title: Map your stakeholders
why_matters: You are about to coordinate work between people who answer to other people. By week three you will be asking one of them for a decision; by week five you'll be asking another to absorb a slip. The stakeholder map is the document that turns those asks from cold calls into conversations you've already started.
steps: Open a fresh document. Use the stakeholder-map template from the Playbook library — at MVP it's a four-column table: Name · Role · Decision rights · Influence.

List every person you've been introduced to as relevant to your programme. Plus the people whose names came up in those introductions but you haven't met yet — flag them with a (?) so you know who to chase a coffee with in week two.
Fill the Decision-rights column honestly. Most rows will be 'consult only' or 'inform only'. The rows where decision rights are unclear are the rows worth a five-minute corridor question in week two.
For the three rows with highest influence, write one sentence underneath: what is this person's pressure right now? (Not what they want from you — what's pressing on *them* this quarter.)
success_criteria: By end of day, the document has every named person you've met or heard about, with Role + Decision-rights filled in. You can name the three people whose pressure shapes whether this programme lands.
reflection_prompt: Of the three high-influence rows, which one's pressure is the one you understand least? What's one thing you could read or ask this week to fix that? Two sentences.
